summary: ELI LILLY AND COMPANY (LEI: FRDRIPF3EKNDJ2CQJL29; Indiana, US) is identifier-confirmed via its LEI, OpenCorporates registration (us_in/183025-143), and Wikidata QID (Q632240). GLEIF Level 2 data reports permitted reporting exceptions for both direct and ultimate accounting-consolidation parent, indicating the entity is controlled by natural persons without an intermediate consolidating legal entity; GLEIF also records at least six direct accounting-consolidation subsidiaries across the US, India, Ireland, the Netherlands, and the UK. David A. Ricks is recorded as CEO and board member (from 2017, per Wikidata) and as an officer (from 2025-01-23, per OpenCorporates), with Jonathan Haug recorded as senior managing official and a large number of additional officers on the Indiana register. Two substantive risk signals require attention: OpenSanctions flags ELI LILLY AND COMPANY itself for trade risk (high confidence, appearing across multiple related-entity matches); and ICIJ Offshore Leaks records associate board member Juan R. Luciano with the Paradise Papers (Barbados corporate registry, ICIJ score 77/100, medium confidence) and officer Christopher Anderson with both the Panama Papers and Paradise Papers (Appleby) (ICIJ score 100/100, high confidence) — all three are name-based matches against the related parties and should be independently verified. Additionally, name-only PEP matches (medium confidence, unconfirmed by birth date or nationality) exist for board member Katherine Baicker (OpenSanctions/EveryPolitician) and officer Patrik Jonsson (OpenSanctions/EveryPolitician). A material gap exists: Wikirate could not be queried due to a source API schema error, so any data that source would have contributed is unavailable.

claims.text: ELI LILLY AND COMPANY is identifier-confirmed, registered in Indiana, United States, with LEI FRDRIPF3EKNDJ2CQJL29, OpenCorporates ID us_in/183025-143, and Wikidata QID Q632240.

GLEIF Level 2 data reports a permitted reporting exception for the direct accounting-consolidation parent, indicating the entity is controlled by natural persons without an intermediate consolidating legal entity.
GLEIF Level 2 data reports the same permitted reporting exception for the ultimate accounting-consolidation parent.

GLEIF records ELI LILLY AND COMPANY as the direct accounting-consolidation parent of at least six subsidiaries: LILLY VENTURES FUND I LLC, ELI LILLY SERVICES INDIA PRIVATE LIMITED, ELI LILLY AND COMPANY (INDIA) PRIVATE LIMITED, ELI LILLY KINSALE LIMITED, Lilly Nederland Finance B.V., and ELI LILLY GROUP PENSION TRUSTEES LIMITED.
David A. Ricks is recorded as CEO and board member of Eli Lilly and Company from 2017-01-01 per Wikidata, and as an officer from 2025-01-23 per OpenCorporates.
Jonathan Haug is recorded as senior managing official from 2023-05-25 per OpenCorporates.

A large number of additional officers are recorded on the Indiana register, including (among others) Patrik Jonsson, Diogo Rau, Jonathan Groff, Katie Lodato, Christopher Anderson, Edgardo Hernandez, Jacob Van Naarden, Anne E. White, Susan Ridlen, Anat Hakim, Daniel Skovronsky, Donald A. Zakrowski, Valorie Wanner, Eric Dozier, Ilya Yuffa, Steffanie R. Lim-Ho, Melissa Seymour, Lucas Montarce, and others.

Board members recorded via Wikidata and/or OpenCorporates include Juan R. Luciano, Karen Walker, Jamere Jackson, Ralph Alvarez, Gabrielle Sulzberger, William G. Kaelin, Kimberly H. Johnson, Katherine Baicker, Mary Lynne Hedley, and Erik Fyrwald.
OpenSanctions flags ELI LILLY AND COMPANY for trade risk (high confidence), with this signal appearing across multiple related-entity matches.

ICIJ Offshore Leaks records associate board member Juan R. Luciano with the Paradise Papers (Barbados corporate registry) at an ICIJ score of 77/100 (medium confidence); this is a name-based match against the related party and requires independent verification.

ICIJ Offshore Leaks records associate officer Christopher Anderson with both the Panama Papers and the Paradise Papers (Appleby) at an ICIJ score of 100/100 (high confidence); these are name-based matches against the related party and require independent verification.
Name-only PEP matches (medium confidence, unconfirmed by birth date or nationality) exist for board member Katherine Baicker via OpenSanctions and EveryPolitician.
Name-only PEP matches (medium confidence, unconfirmed by birth date or nationality) exist for officer Patrik Jonsson via OpenSanctions and EveryPolitician.
Wikirate could not be queried due to a source API schema error, so any data that source would have contributed is unavailable.

limitations: Wikirate could not be queried (source API schema error affecting headquarters and website fields), leaving any Wikirate-sourced data absent from this review (g1).

Officer and board-member data from Wikidata is sourced from a crowd-sourced knowledge base and should be treated as indicative rather than authoritative; no start/end dates are confirmed by an official register.

All ICIJ Offshore Leaks matches (Juan R. Luciano, Christopher Anderson) and PEP matches (Katherine Baicker, Patrik Jonsson) are name-based only, with no corroborating identifiers (birth date, nationality) — positive identification of the related parties with the screened individuals has not been established.
GLEIF Level 2 records accounting consolidation, not beneficial ownership; the natural-persons reporting exception means no named beneficial owners are disclosed in the LEI record.
One Wikidata board-member record (f12) is identified only by a Wikidata QID (Q105798427) with no resolved name available in the packet.

risks.label: No parent in GLEIF (permitted reporting exception)
risks.rationale: No accounting-consolidation parent is reported to GLEIF: NATURAL_PERSONS for the direct and ultimate parent (the entity is controlled directly by natural person(s), with no intermediate legal entity that consolidates it — common for founder-, family-owned and widely held companies). Structural context, not a risk finding — these are permitted exceptions under the LEI ROC policy, and GLEIF Level 2 records accounting consolidation, not beneficial ownership.

risks.label: Outside EU/EEA
risks.rationale: Ownership chain reaches jurisdictions outside the EU/EEA: GB, IN, US-DE, US-IN. Structural context, not a risk finding — neither the AMLA CDD RTS nor AMLR Annex III treats non-EU status as a risk factor in itself. Contributes to AMLA Article 12(1) condition (b) only where it appears on the layered ownership path.
